problem: The exponential is written as "[A] = [A]₀ e−kt", with no superscript. Read literally this is e minus k·t, which is not the integrated rate law and will mislead a student reading on a phone.
fix: Write [A] = [A]₀ e<sup>−kt</sup> (equivalently [A] = [A]₀ exp(−kt)), and say k is in s⁻¹ and t in s.

problem: "Instantaneous rate is the slope of the concentration-time graph at one instant." For a reactant that slope is negative, yet the rate was just defined with a minus sign to make it positive; the two statements contradict each other as written.
fix: Say: for a reactant, instantaneous rate = −(slope of the tangent to the concentration-time curve); the slope itself is negative.

problem: "Some syllabi call order reaction order and molecularity elementary molecularity" is a tautology and adds no information; the second half is not a standard usage and confuses students.
fix: Delete the sentence. Keep only: order is sometimes called reaction order, while molecularity applies to one elementary step and has no meaning for an overall reaction.

problem: "Molecularity is the number of species colliding in one elementary step" is loose: a unimolecular step has molecularity 1 and involves no collision at all.
fix: Molecularity is the number of reactant species that take part in one elementary step: 1 for a unimolecular step, 2 for a bimolecular step. It is a mechanism count and is always a whole number.

problem: Only the method of initial rates is given. Exam questions also ask for order from concentration-time data, and the chapter never says how to get it, even though the three integrated laws are already stated in Section 2.
fix: Add one line: order can also be found graphically — plot [A] against t, ln[A] against t, and 1/[A] against t; the plot that is a straight line gives the order (0, 1 and 2 respectively), and the slope gives k.
